items.title: TTL Cache
items.text:
An LRU cache decorator with a time to live. ttl_lru_cache works exactly like functools.lru_cache, except entries automatically expire after a configurable number of seconds.

Basic usage
from ttl_cache import ttl_lru_cache


@ttl_lru_cache(ttl=30)  # (1)!
def fetch_user(user_id: int) -> dict:
    print("Fetching from the network...")
    return {"id": user_id, "name": "Ada"}


fetch_user(1)  # Prints "Fetching from the network..."
fetch_user(1)  # Cache hit, nothing printed
# ... 30 seconds later ...
fetch_user(1)  # Expired — fetches again
  1. Cache results for 30 seconds. While the TTL window is open, repeat calls with the same arguments are served from the cache.

items.title: ttl_lru_cache
items.text:
ttl_lru_cache(ttl=60, jitter=0, maxsize=128, typed=False)

A decorator that works like lru_cache but with a time to live (ttl).

Under the hood it still uses lru_cache, but the cached call receives an extra positional-only time_bucket argument:

time_bucket = int((time.monotonic() + offset) // ttl)

An entry stays "alive" while the bucket value is unchanged and expires when the bucket rolls over. offset is drawn once per decorated function from random.uniform(0, jitter), so different functions (or processes) expire at different moments instead of all at once.

Time to live in seconds. Defaults to 60.

0 maxsize int | None

Max size of the cache, or None for unbounded. Defaults to 128.

128 typed bool

Whether argument types are part of the cache key. Defaults to False.

>>> @ttl_lru_cache(ttl=30, jitter=5)

def ttl_lru_cache[**P, R](
    ttl: float = 60,
    jitter: float = 0,
    maxsize: int | None = 128,
    typed: bool = False,
) -> Callable[[Callable[P, R]], TTLCachedFunction[P, R]]:
    """A decorator that works like ``lru_cache`` but with a time to live (ttl).

    Under the hood it still uses ``lru_cache``, but the cached call receives an
    extra positional-only ``time_bucket`` argument:

        time_bucket = int((time.monotonic() + offset) // ttl)

    An entry stays "alive" while the bucket value is unchanged and expires when
    the bucket rolls over. ``offset`` is drawn once per decorated function from
    ``random.uniform(0, jitter)``, so different functions (or processes) expire
    at different moments instead of all at once.

    Args:
        ttl: Time to live in seconds. Defaults to 60.
        jitter: Max random offset in seconds applied to the bucket boundaries.
            Defaults to 0.
        maxsize: Max size of the cache, or ``None`` for unbounded. Defaults to 128.
        typed: Whether argument types are part of the cache key. Defaults to False.

    Returns:
        A decorator that wraps a function in a TTL-aware LRU cache. The wrapped
        function keeps its signature and exposes ``cache_info`` and
        ``cache_clear``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``ttl`` is not positive or ``jitter`` is negative.

    Example:

        >>> @ttl_lru_cache(ttl=30, jitter=5)
        ... def fetch(key: str) -> str:
        ...     return key.upper()
    """
    if ttl <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"ttl must be positive, got {ttl!r}")
    if jitter < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"jitter must be non-negative, got {jitter!r}")

    def decorator(func: Callable[P, R]) -> TTLCachedFunction[P, R]:
        offset = random.uniform(0, jitter)

        @lru_cache(maxsize=maxsize, typed=typed)
        def cached_with_time(_time_bucket: int, /, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> R:
            return func(*args, **kwargs)

        # lru_cache types its arguments as Hashable, which P.args/P.kwargs can't
        # be proven to be. Unhashable arguments still raise TypeError at call
        # time, exactly as with plain lru_cache.
        call_cached = cast(Callable[..., R], cached_with_time)

        @wraps(func)
        def wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> R:
            time_bucket = int((time.monotonic() + offset) // ttl)
            return call_cached(time_bucket, *args, **kwargs)

        wrapper.__dict__.update(
            cache_info=cached_with_time.cache_info,
            cache_clear=cached_with_time.cache_clear,
        )
        return cast(TTLCachedFunction[P, R], wrapper)

    return decorator

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Under the hood it still uses lru_cache, but the cached call receives an extra positional-only time bucket argument derived from a monotonic clock:

The time bucket
time_bucket = int((time.monotonic() + offset) // ttl)

An entry stays "alive" while the bucket value is unchanged and expires when the bucket rolls over:

graph LR
  A[Call] --> B{Bucket changed?}
  B -->|No| C[Serve cached value]
  B -->|Yes| D[Recompute and cache]
  C --> E[Return]
  D --> E

Note

The bucket boundary is shared per TTL window, so an entry lives for at most ttl seconds and at least the remainder of the current bucket.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
pipuv 
pip install ttl-cache-decorator

uv add ttl-cache-decorator

Requires Python 3.12+. Works on all major platforms including Windows, macOS, and Linux.
